title: Victim compensation scheme - an underused remedy in criminal cases
p1:
Many victims of crime fight for justice but never claim a benefit they may already be entitled to.

A criminal case does not always end with punishment for the offender. There may also be a path to support the person who suffered the harm.
p2:
A common misconception is that compensation is only available through a private lawsuit or by recovering money from the accused.

In reality, many legal systems have victim compensation schemes where eligible victims can seek financial assistance from the state, especially when crime has caused injury, loss, or serious hardship.
p3:
This remedy is often overlooked because people focus only on conviction and punishment. But compensation can help with medical expenses, rehabilitation, loss of income, or rebuilding life after a traumatic event.

The practical takeaway: after reporting a crime, victims should explore every available legal remedy, not just the criminal trial outcome.
conclusion: Did you know that a victim may have a right to compensation even when recovering money directly from the offender is difficult? Should more people be made aware of this remedy?
